findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy (CSP) Header
findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an effective layer of defense against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), data injection, and unauthorized frame embedding.
findings.evidence: Header 'Content-Security-Policy' was not found in response.
findings.impact: Leaves client vulnerable to Stored, Reflected, and DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
findings.remediation: Define a restrictive CSP such as: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none';

findings.title: Missing Clickjacking Defense (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
findings.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors is present to restrict iframe embedding.
findings.evidence: Neither X-Frame-Options nor frame-ancestors found in response headers.
findings.impact: Allows malicious sites to embed target inside hidden iframes to conduct Clickjacking attacks.
findings.remediation: Set 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN', or use CSP 'frame-ancestors' directive.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options Header
findings.description: The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header prevents the browser from MIME-sniffing a response away from the declared content-type, preventing executable content execution in non-executable formats.
findings.impact: Browsers may execute malicious user-uploaded content (e.g. SVG or images parsed as HTML/JS).

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy Header
findings.description: Referrer-Policy governs what referrer information sent in the Referer header should be included with requests made.
findings.impact: Sensitive URL query parameters (tokens, session IDs) may be leaked to third-party domains.

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy Header
findings.description: Permissions-Policy allows site administrators to declare which browser features and APIs (e.g., geolocation, camera, microphone, payment) can be used by the page and embedded iframes.
findings.impact: Third-party embedded scripts or iframes could attempt to access sensitive hardware APIs.
findings.remediation: Add header: Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()

findings.title: Server Technology Information Disclosure (Server)
findings.description: Server exposes technology header 'server' containing 'BaseHTTP/0.6 Python/3.13.6, Apache/2.4.41 (Ubuntu) OpenSSL/1.1.1'.
findings.impact: Revealing backend software frameworks and versions assists attackers in fingerprinting known CVE vulnerabilities and tailoring exploit payloads.
findings.remediation: Disable, strip, or mask the 'server' header in reverse proxy or web server config.

findings.title: Server Technology Information Disclosure (X-Powered-By)
findings.impact: Revealing backend software frameworks and versions assists attackers in fingerprinting known CVE vulnerabilities and tailoring exploit payloads.
findings.remediation: Disable, strip, or mask the 'x-powered-by' header in reverse proxy or web server config.

findings.title: Critical CORS Vulnerability: Reflected Origin with Credentials (Arbitrary Third-Party Origin Reflection)
findings.description: The endpoint dynamically reflects the provided Origin header 'https://evil-attacker.com' in 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' AND explicitly enables 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. This effectively disables the browser Same-Origin Policy (SOP).
findings.evidence:
Request Origin: https://evil-attacker.com
Response Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil-attacker.com
Response Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
findings.impact: An attacker hosting malicious JavaScript on an external site can make authenticated XMLHttpRequest / Fetch requests to this endpoint using the victim's session cookies or HTTP auth headers, and read sensitive confidential responses.
findings.remediation: Do NOT dynamically reflect the Origin header. Maintain a strict server-side whitelist of authorized domains. Never set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true unless the origin is strictly verified.

headers_audit.name: Strict-Transport-Security
headers_audit.details: Not applicable on plain HTTP endpoints. HSTS should be enforced once redirected to HTTPS.
headers_audit.recommendation: Enforce HTTPS redirect and configure Strict-Transport-Security.

headers_audit.name: Content-Security-Policy
headers_audit.details: Missing. Target provides no CSP mitigation against Cross-Site Scripting.
headers_audit.recommendation: Implement a robust CSP policy restricting script and object sources.

headers_audit.name: X-Content-Type-Options
headers_audit.details: Missing. MIME sniffing protection is disabled.

headers_audit.name: Referrer-Policy
headers_audit.details: Missing. Default browser fallback will be used.

headers_audit.name: Permissions-Policy
headers_audit.details: Missing modern browser hardware/API restriction header.

headers_audit.name: Cross-Origin-Isolation (COOP/COEP)
headers_audit.details: Not configured. Modern defense against Spectre side-channel attacks and tab-nabbing.

headers_audit.name: Server
headers_audit.details: Banner leakage: exposes Server Software & Version.

headers_audit.name: X-Powered-By
headers_audit.details: Banner leakage: exposes Application Technology / Framework.
